pullpoints: The refugee representation debate is inseparable from the historical unity and political identity of the State of Jammu & Kashmir.
Abolishing refugee seats risks legitimizing the permanent division of the state and undermining international legal principles.
Artificial narratives of 'local vs. refugee' are being weaponized to divide Kashmiris and derail their collective political struggle.
Political instability in AJK could threaten the constitutional system and open the door to non-democratic interventions.

body.text: Jammu Kashmir Refugee Representation in AJK, State Unity, and Our Political Disorientation

A contentious and fresh debate is currently emerging within Azad Jammu and Kashmir regarding the reserved seats and political representation of Jammu and Kashmir refugees in the Legislative Assembly...
“The refugee question is not a constitutional formality — it is a question of identity, history, and political continuity.”
Historical Roots of Displacement

The historical and undeniable reality is that prior to August 15, 1947, the entire State of Jammu and Kashmir including Jammu, Ladakh, the Valley, Gilgit-Baltistan, and present-day Azad Kashmir was an indivisible political and geographical entity...
“Displacement does not erase state identity — nor does it strip citizens of their political rights.”

“To abolish refugee seats is to accept the forced partition of Jammu & Kashmir as permanent.”

About the Author

Sardar Shaukat Ali Kashmiri is the Chairman of the United Kashmir People's National Party (UKPNP), a secular and progressive Kashmiri political leader and renowned human rights defender. Originally from Trarkhel Sudhanoti, Azad Kashmir, he is currently based in Switzerland and has spent decades advocating for peace, justice, state unity, and the political rights of the forcibly divided people of Jammu & Kashmir.
